title: Validate fast Undo while Clear-list delegates are retiring
environment: Qt 6.12 Windows Qt Quick Test, native/offscreen. Android touch controls pass.
finding: Early coverage tests sometimes lost Undo history when tapping before outgoing delegates had retired. This was initially classified too strongly as a confirmed Clear-list bug.
current_evidence: Waiting for all short-fixture delegates to match the current model count and finish moving makes normal editor entry and both mouse/touch Clear/Undo pass without application changes. Full flip angle alone was not sufficient input readiness.
reproduction_status: No confirmed defect in the settled user path. Fast input during the transition still needs a rendered-hit-target reproduction before assigning bug severity or implementing an app fix.
reproduction_to_collect: Clear a list, then capture an actual pointer press on the visibly offered Undo icon while outgoing delegates remain.
Record the rendered state and receiver of the press; distinguish a retiring row intercepting input from the Undo button receiving it.
Compare with the fully settled control on Windows and Android.
expected: A settled Undo control restores removed names, ordering, flags and IDs. Establish the intended/actual behavior for an interruption during the animation before declaring another defect.
tests: tests/flows/tst_userflows.qml: UserFlows::test_drawer_removal:all_mouse and :all_touch retain full restoration assertions; no XFAIL or skip remains.
tests/android/test_reset.py --case clear verifies real native touch Undo, including saved order/checks/IDs.
history: Earlier flows-stable.txt/undo-final-native.txt failures and expected-failure runs lacked whole-list settlement. They are investigation evidence, superseded as acceptance results by the final readiness-aware runs.
implementation_scope: No application fix is authorized or implemented for this candidate. Keep investigation separate from QA-003 test-driver changes.
